title_en: Liquidation Group of Wenzhou Trust Company v. Xingfu Industrial Company, et al. — dispute over contract for assignment of creditor's rights and debts
keywords_en: Civil; dispute over contract for transfer of creditor's rights and debts; second instance; Supreme People's Court; Zhejiang Province; Hubei Province; legal person; financial institution; Guarantee Law; validity of guarantee contract; company providing guarantee for its shareholder; authenticity of seal; reversal of judgment; transfer of creditor's rights; guarantee; seal authentication; contract dispute; company, etc. dispute over transfer of creditor's rights and debts
full_text_en:
Wenzhou Trust Company Liquidation Group v. Xingfu Industrial Co., Ltd. et al. — dispute over debt and creditor's rights transfer contract

Ruling Summary

Where a joint stock company uses its assets to provide a guarantee for its own shareholder, the guarantee contract is void. If the creditor and the guarantor are at fault, the portion of civil liability borne by the guarantor shall not exceed one-half of the portion of the debt that the debtor fails to repay.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court
(2002) Min Er Zhong Zi No. 67

Appellant (Plaintiff at First Instance): Liquidation Group of Wenzhou International Trust and Investment Company, domiciled at Floors 22-23, Guoxin Building, East Renmin Road, Wenzhou City, Zhejiang Province.
Responsible Person: Cai Yongjin, Head of the Liquidation Group.
Agent ad litem: Qu Shaojun, Attorney at Zhejiang Jiaruicheng Law Firm.
Agent ad litem: Huang Yuejun, Attorney at Zhejiang Jiaruicheng Law Firm.

Appellee (Defendant at First Instance): Hubei Xingfu Industrial Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 1 Xingfu North Road, Zhangjin Town, Qianjiang City, Hubei Province.
Legal Representative: Liu Daoming, Chairman of the Board.
Agent ad litem: Wang Guiyun, Attorney at Beijing Fada Law Firm.

Defendant at First Instance: Xingfu Group Company, domiciled at No. 1 Xingfu North Road, Zhangjin Town, Qianjiang City, Hubei Province.
Legal Representative: Lin Fasong, General Manager of the Company.
Agent ad litem: Lin Zhiqing, Deputy General Manager of the Company.
Agent ad litem: Gao Hansheng, Attorney at Hubei Jianghan Law Firm.

The appellant, Liquidation Group of Wenzhou International Trust and Investment Company, appealed to this Court against the civil judgment (2001) E Jing Chu Zi No. 22 rendered by the High People's Court of Hubei Province in the case of dispute over a debt and creditor's rights transfer contract with the appellee, Hubei Xingfu Industrial Co., Ltd., and the defendant at first instance, Xingfu Group Company. This Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law, with Judge Song Xiaoming serving as presiding judge, and Judges Wu Qingbao and Acting Judge Liu Min participating in the deliberation, and Court Clerk Yin Jing keeping the record. The trial of this case has now been concluded.

The following facts were found:

On November 3, 1998, a "Debt and Creditor's Rights Transfer Agreement" was signed by the following four parties, as named: Hubei Provincial International Trust and Investment Company (hereinafter referred to as Hubei Guotou, Party A), Wenzhou International Trust and Investment Company (hereinafter referred to as Wenzhou Guotou, Party B), Xingfu Group Company (hereinafter referred to as the Group Company, Party C), and Hubei Xingfu Industrial Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as the Industrial Company, Party D). The agreement stipulated: Wenzhou Guotou, Hubei Guotou, and the Group Company unanimously agreed to transfer USD 3,600,000 of Hubei Guotou's creditor's rights against the Group Company (based on the civil mediation documents (1997) E Jing Chu Zi Nos. 89 and 90 of the High People's Court of Hubei Province) to Wenzhou Guotou, in order to settle all creditor-debtor relationships between Wenzhou Guotou and Hubei Guotou. After the execution of this agreement, Wenzhou Guotou would hold a creditor's right of USD 3,600,000 against the Group Company; the creditor-debtor relationship between Wenzhou Guotou and Hubei Guotou would be terminated; and simultaneously, the creditor-debtor relationship of USD 3,600,000 between the Group Company and Hubei Guotou would also be terminated. From the effective date of this agreement until the date of full repayment, interest on Wenzhou Guotou's creditor's right of USD 3,600,000 against the Group Company would accrue at an annual rate of 8.4%, with interest to be settled together with the principal debt. The Group Company was to repay all debts by December 31, 1999. If the Group Company could not fully repay this debt by December 31, 1999, it must unconditionally, by the end of March 2000, transfer to Wenzhou Guotou a corresponding number of legal person shares of the Industrial Company held by the Group Company to offset all outstanding debts. The transfer price per share would be calculated based on the diluted net asset value per share published in the Industrial Company's 1999 annual report. The Group Company was responsible for handling the transfer and registration of the shares. Upon completion of the transfer, the transfer expenses would be borne by the Industrial Company. If the Group Company failed to repay the debt within the aforementioned time limit, in addition to continuing to pay interest to Wenzhou Guotou at an annual rate of 8.4%, from the date of default, it would also bear a daily penalty of 0.05% on the outstanding amount until full repayment. The Industrial Company voluntarily assumed irrevocable joint and several liability as a guarantor for the Group Company's performance of the debts under this agreement, with the guarantee period commencing from the date of signing of this agreement until December 31, 2001. The scope of the guarantee included the principal of USD 3,600,000, interest, penalties, and related litigation costs, enforcement costs, and attorney fees. It further guaranteed that if the Group Company could not repay Wenzhou Guotou's debt on time, the guarantor would ensure that the Group Company completed the transfer procedures for the legal person shares of the Industrial Company corresponding to the debt amount. After the transfer, the remaining creditor's rights of Hubei Guotou against the Group Company would be resolved separately by Hubei Guotou and the Group Company. The agreement would take effect immediately upon being stamped by all four parties and signed by their legal representatives (or authorized representatives). Wenzhou Guotou, Hubei Guotou, and the Group Company signed and stamped the agreement in the columns for Parties A, B, and C respectively. In the column for Party D, i.e., the Industrial Company, the seal affixed was that of "Hubei Xingfu (Group) Industrial Co., Ltd.", and the signatory was Luo Bangliang.

It was also found that on November 3, 1998, Luo Bangliang, Director of the Qianjiang City Xingfu Urban Credit Cooperative in Hubei Province, signed the aforementioned "Debt and Creditor's Rights Transfer Agreement" holding a "Power of Attorney" bearing the seal of "Hubei Xingfu (Group) Industrial Co., Ltd." and the private seal of "Zhou Zuoliang's Seal", with the content: "Hereby authorize Luo Bangliang to represent our company in signing the debt and creditor's rights transfer agreement with Hubei Guotou and Wenzhou Guotou."

Regarding the seals of "Hubei Xingfu (Group) Industrial Co., Ltd." affixed to the aforementioned "Debt and Creditor's Rights Transfer Agreement" and "Power of Attorney", during the first instance of this case, the Judicial Technical Department of the High People's Court of Hubei Province conducted a forensic examination, with the conclusion: the seal affixed to the transfer agreement was not the same seal as the one used before the change of the Industrial Company's name and filed with the administrative department for industry and commerce. During the second instance, the appellant, Wenzhou Guotou, submitted to this Court an expert opinion from the Judicial Identification Center of the Ministry of Justice, which it had commissioned for a second examination of the two seals. The conclusion of this examination was that the impressions of the two seals were identical to the impression of "Hubei Xingfu (Group) Industrial Co., Ltd." left on the 1997 "Profit and Profit Distribution Statement of Joint Stock Enterprise Accounting Reports". However, this sample material was a photocopy. On May 25, 2002, Wenzhou Guotou further submitted a document examination application to this Court, requesting an examination of the seals affixed to the 1997 "Profit and Profit Distribution Statement of Joint Stock Enterprise Accounting Reports", the seal on the cover of the October 25, 1998 financial statistics report of the Industrial Company, and the seal affixed to the November 3, 1998 "Debt and Creditor's Rights Transfer Agreement". However, the sample materials submitted to this Court were still photocopies, with the application noting that the originals were respectively held by the Hubei Provincial Administration for Industry and Commerce and the Group Company.

It was further found: The Industrial Company was originally named Hubei Xingfu (Group) Industrial Co., Ltd. On May 17, 1998, it applied for a change of registration with the administrative department for industry and commerce, changing its name to the Industrial Company. On May 18, 1998, the administrative department for industry and commerce issued a business license for an enterprise legal person under the name of the Industrial Company. At the time of signing the "Debt and Creditor's Rights Transfer Agreement", the legal representatives of both the Group Company and the Industrial Company were Zhou Zuoliang. The Group Company was the largest shareholder of the Industrial Company, and Hubei Guotou was among the top ten shareholders of the Industrial Company. On October 25, 1999, after the Group Company offset part of its legal person shares in the Industrial Company to Hubei Guotou, Hubei Guotou became the largest shareholder of the Industrial Company. On August 1, 2000, Mingliu Investment Co., Ltd. acquired part of the legal person shares of the Industrial Company through auction and became the largest shareholder of the Industrial Company.

In the 1999 "Annual Report" of the Industrial Company, in section 7, item 7, "Major Related Party Transactions", and in section 8, "Financial Accounting Report", item 9, "Contingent Matters and Commitments", it was stated: On November 3, 1998, the Group Company, the Industrial Company, Wenzhou Guotou, and Hubei Guotou signed a four-party debt and creditor's rights transfer agreement, confirming that the Group Company owed Wenzhou Guotou USD 3,600,000, and the Industrial Company assumed irrevocable joint and several guarantee liability for the USD 3,600,000 and interest for the Group Company. Additionally, because the "three separations" (of personnel, finance, and assets) between the Industrial Company and its original largest shareholder, the Group Company, had not yet been completed, other mortgage and guarantee matters were still under review.

On July 5, 2000, Wenzhou Guotou, on the grounds that the Group Company had neither handled the share transfer procedures nor repaid the debt, and that the Industrial Company had also failed to perform its guarantee obligations, filed a lawsuit with the High People's Court of Hubei Province, requesting the court to order the Group Company to repay the debt of USD 3,600,000 and interest of USD 355,320, plus overdue interest of USD 320,400 (calculated up to June 26, 2000); to order the Industrial Company to bear joint and several liability; and to order the defendants to bear the litigation costs and related expenses.

After trial, the High People's Court of Hubei Province held that: the debt and creditor's rights transfer agreement signed by Wenzhou Guotou, Hubei Guotou, and the Group Company was the true intent of the three parties and the transfer agreement was valid. Although the Industrial Company's name appeared on the transfer agreement, the seal affixed in the guarantor column was neither the seal of the Industrial Company nor the seal that was lawfully used and filed with the administrative department for industry and commerce before the change of the Industrial Company's name. Moreover, the signatory on the transfer agreement, Luo Bangliang, was the Director of the Qianjiang City Xingfu Urban Credit Cooperative in Hubei Province, not a staff member of the Industrial Company. The "Power of Attorney" he held bore the seal "Zhou Zuoliang's Seal", which was also not the "Zhou Zuoliang Seal" used by Zhou Zuoliang as the legal representative of the Industrial Company. Therefore, the seal affixed by the Industrial Company as a guarantor on the transfer agreement was not its true intent, and the guarantee relationship between it and Wenzhou Guotou was not established. Wenzhou Guotou's claim for the Industrial Company to bear joint and several liability for the Group Company's debt should be dismissed. After agreeing to the transfer of Hubei Guotou's creditor's rights against it to Wenzhou Guotou, the Group Company failed to perform its repayment obligations within the period specified in the transfer agreement, constituting a breach of contract and should bear full responsibility for the dispute in this case. Pursuant to Article 111 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China and Article 128 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the court rendered the following judgment: 1. The Group Company shall repay Wenzhou Guotou the principal debt of USD 3,600,000. 2. The Group Company shall pay Wenzhou Guotou interest on the USD 3,600,000 (calculated from November 3, 1998 to March 31, 2000, at the one-year USD lending rate of the People's Bank of China for the corresponding period; and from April 1, 2000 until the date of full payment, at the penalty interest rate for overdue USD loans of the People's Bank of China for the corresponding period). 3. Wenzhou Guotou's claim against the Industrial Company is dismissed. The first-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 195,010 and the litigation preservation fee of RMB 185,520 shall be borne by the Group Company.

Dissatisfied with the above civil judgment of the High People's Court of Hubei Province, Wenzhou Guotou appealed to this Court, stating: 1. After changing its name, the Industrial Company continued to use the seal used before the name change, and there was a fact that multiple seals were used simultaneously. Therefore, all seals in use by the Industrial Company should be verified. The conclusion of the forensic examination by the court of first instance was not exclusive or unique and could not serve as the basis for deciding the case. The original judgment's conclusion that the stamping of the seal by the Industrial Company on the transfer agreement was not its true intent, based solely on the fact that the Industrial Company's seal on the "Debt and Creditor's Rights Transfer Agreement" was not the same seal as the one filed with the Industrial and Commercial Bureau before the name change, is unsustainable. The appellant had submitted sample impressions (photocopies) and opinions on re-examination to the court of first instance, but these were not given due consideration or adopted. During the second instance, the Judicial Identification Center of the Ministry of Justice conducted an examination of the seal impressions, and the result showed that the seals on the transfer agreement and the power of attorney were identical to the seal on the 1997 company profit and profit distribution statement. Zhou Zuoliang was both the legal representative of the Group Company and the Industrial Company. Whether the private seals "Zhou Zuoliang's Seal" and "Zhou Zuoliang Seal" respectively represented the Group Company and the Industrial Company was an internal distinction and had no legal significance externally. Zhou Zuoliang's authorization of Luo Bangliang to sign the agreement was his true intent. The original judgment's reasoning that Luo Bangliang was not a staff member of the Industrial Company, used as one of the grounds for concluding that the guarantee was not established, lacks legal basis. 2. The Industrial Company's 1999 annual report truthfully disclosed the guarantee matter in this case, which should be considered valid evidence confirming its status as a guarantor. The court of first instance failed to recognize this. 3. The effective condition of the "Debt and Creditor's Rights Transfer Agreement" was the stamping and signing by all four parties and their legal representatives. Therefore, even if, as the first-instance judgment held, the stamping of the seal by the Industrial Company as a guarantor on the transfer agreement was not its true intent, the entire "Debt and Creditor's Rights Transfer Agreement" should be deemed ineffective, rather than only the guarantee of the Industrial Company being invalid while the debt transfer was valid. 4. Not only did the court of first instance err in finding facts, but its determination of the validity of the "Debt and Creditor's Rights Transfer Agreement" under the facts it found was also erroneous. The appellant requests the court of second instance to amend the judgment in accordance with law.

The appellee, the Industrial Company, argued in its defense: The seals of the guarantor affixed to the "Debt and Creditor's Rights Transfer Agreement" and the "Power of Attorney" were not the seal of the Industrial Company, nor were they valid seals ever used by the Industrial Company. At the time of signing the transfer agreement, no representative of the Industrial Company was present. The private seal of the legal representative on the "Power of Attorney" was also not the private seal of the legal representative of the Industrial Company. When signing the transfer agreement, Wenzhou Guotou knew or should have known that the guarantor was not the Industrial Company, yet it still stamped and signed the agreement. It should bear responsibility for its own fault. Although the 1999 annual report of the Industrial Company mentioned the four-party agreement under contingent matters, this was learned from Wenzhou Guotou's letter demanding performance of the guarantee obligation, and did not constitute acknowledgment or acceptance of the guarantee. Moreover, in the 2000 annual report, the Industrial Company clearly stated that it did not recognize the agreement and would seek resolution through legal means. Even if the Industrial Company had signed the agreement, since the Group Company was at that time the largest shareholder of the Industrial Company, under the Company Law, a joint stock company providing a guarantee for its shareholder would be void. Wenzhou Guotou's application for a new forensic examination does not comply with the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Evidence in Civil Proceedings and should be dismissed. The judgment of the court of first instance was correct and should be affirmed.

In the opinion of this Court: Although there is currently insufficient evidence to prove that the seal of "Hubei Xingfu (Group) Industrial Co., Ltd." affixed to the "Debt and Creditor's Rights Transfer Agreement" dated November 3, 1998, signed by Wenzhou Guotou, Hubei Guotou, the Group Company, and the Industrial Company, was the genuine seal of the Industrial Company, the 1999 annual report of the Industrial Company, in the sections "Major Related Party Transactions" and "Contingent Matters and Commitments" of the financial accounting report, clearly states: "On November 3, 1998, the Group Company, the Industrial Company, Wenzhou Guotou, and Hubei Guotou signed a four-party debt and creditor's rights transfer agreement, confirming that the Group Company owed Wenzhou Guotou USD 3,600,000, and the Industrial Company assumed irrevocable joint and several guarantee liability for the USD 3,600,000 and interest for the Group Company." From the content of the above annual report of the Industrial Company, the Industrial Company should have been aware of its provision of a guarantee for Wenzhou Guotou, and there is currently no evidence that the Industrial Company raised any objection to the provision of the guarantee at that time. The parties have no objection to the formal authenticity of the above annual report, which should be admitted as evidence. Therefore, the provision by the Industrial Company of a guarantee for Wenzhou Guotou's principal of USD 3,600,000 and interest should be deemed as its true intention at the time, and the Industrial Company should bear corresponding civil liability for this debt. This Court will no longer conduct an examination of the several seals submitted by the appellant. The appellant's ground of appeal, that the court of first instance erred in concluding that the stamping by the Industrial Company in the guarantor column of the transfer agreement was not its true intent based solely on the fact that the guarantor's seal on the transfer agreement was not the seal of the Industrial Company nor the seal lawfully used and filed with the administrative department for industry and commerce before the change of the Industrial Company's name, is supported by this Court. At the time of signing the "Debt and Creditor's Rights Transfer Agreement", Zhou Zuoliang was the legal representative of both the Group Company and the Industrial Company. Whether his two private seals, "Zhou Zuoliang's Seal" and "Zhou Zuoliang Seal", respectively represented the Group Company and the Industrial Company was merely an internal distinction and had no legally binding effect externally. The determination by the court of first instance that the "Zhou Zuoliang's Seal" affixed to the "Power of Attorney" held by Luo Bangliang represented only the Group Company and not the Industrial Company was improper. Pursuant to Article 60 of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China, which provides: "Directors and managers shall not use the company's assets to provide guarantees for the company's shareholders or for the personal debts of other persons," and Article 4 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Certain Issues Concerning the Application of the Guarantee Law of the People's Republic of China, which provides: "Where a director or manager, in violation of Article 60 of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China, uses the company's assets to provide a guarantee for the company's shareholder or for the personal debts of another person, the guarantee contract is void. Except where the creditor knew or should have known, the debtor and the guarantor shall bear joint and several liability for compensation for the creditor's losses," since the Group Company was the largest shareholder of the Industrial Company at that time, the guarantee provided by the Industrial Company for the Group Company should be determined to be void. Because the transfer agreement explicitly provides that if the Group Company cannot repay the debt to Wenzhou Guotou when due, the legal person shares of the Industrial Company held by the Group Company shall be used to offset the debt, the creditor Wenzhou Guotou should have known that the Industrial Company was providing a guarantee for its shareholder, the Group Company. Given that both Wenzhou Guotou and the Industrial Company violated legally prohibited provisions in signing the guarantee contract and both are at fault for the invalidity of the guarantee, pursuant to Article 7 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Certain Issues Concerning the Application of the Guarantee Law of the People's Republic of China, which provides: "Where the principal contract is valid but the guarantee contract is void, if the creditor is without fault, the guarantor and the debtor shall bear joint and several liability for compensation for the economic losses of the creditor under the principal contract; if the creditor and the guarantor are at fault, the portion of civil liability borne by the guarantor shall not exceed one-half of the portion of the debt that the debtor fails to repay," for the losses caused by the invalidity of the guarantee, i.e., the portion of the debt that the debtor Group Company fails to repay, the Industrial Company shall bear compensation liability within the range of 50%, and the remaining losses shall be borne by Wenzhou Guotou itself.

In summary, pursuant to Article 153, paragraph 1, item (3) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, this Court renders the following judgment:

1. Item 1 and Item 2 of the main text of the civil judgment (2001) E Jing Chu Zi No. 22 of the High People's Court of Hubei Province, as well as the allocation of the first-instance case acceptance fee and litigation preservation fee, are affirmed.

2. Item 3 of the main text of the above civil judgment is reversed.

3. Hubei Xingfu Industrial Co., Ltd. shall bear compensation liability for the portion of the debt that Xingfu Group Company fails to repay in this case, within the range of 50%.

The above payable amounts shall be performed within 10 days from the day following the service of this judgment. In case of delayed performance, the provisions of Article 232 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China shall apply. The second-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 195,010.00 shall be borne by Wenzhou International Trust and Investment Company in the amount of RMB 97,505.00 and by Hubei Xingfu Industrial Co., Ltd. in the amount of RMB 97,505.00.

This judgment is final.

Presiding Judge: Song Xiaoming
Judge: Wu Qingbao
Acting Judge: Liu Min

July 18, 2002

Clerk of Court: Yin Jing

Brief Introduction of the Presiding Judge

Song Xiaoming, Senior Judge: Born in 1959, Master of Laws. Since 2002, served as Deputy Chief Judge of the Second Civil Division of the Supreme People's Court.
